It is completely normal to feel hesitant about sharing explicit content, even with a close friend. Reading explicit fanfiction (often referred to as "NSFW" or "smut" in online communities) is a common but highly private activity, and sharing it can sometimes feel vulnerable or awkward. 

If you are trying to decide whether to share the link, here are a few practical factors to consider:

### 1. Your Own Comfort Level
Your privacy and comfort are the most important factors. If sharing the link makes you feel exposed, self-conscious, or uncomfortable, you are under no obligation to do so. It is entirely okay to keep your reading preferences private. You can simply tell your friend, "I'd actually prefer to keep this one to myself," or offer to share a different, less explicit story instead.

### 2. Your Friend's Comfort Level and Expectations
Even if your friend asked for the link, highly explicit content can sometimes catch people off guard if they do not know exactly what to expect. If you do decide to share it, it can be helpful to give them a clear heads-up first. For example, you could say, "Just so you know, this fic gets really explicit/NSFW, so make sure you're comfortable with that before you open it." This allows your friend to make an informed choice.

### 3. Communication Channels and Platform Rules
Be mindful of the platform you use to send the link. Some messaging apps, school-monitored devices or accounts, and social media platforms have strict filters or terms of service regarding the sharing of explicit links. Sending certain links through these channels can sometimes flag an account or violate user agreements.

Ultimately, there is no right or wrong answer, and the decision depends on your personal boundaries and the nature of your friendship. Taking a moment to pause and consider your comfort level is a very healthy way to handle the situation.

It is **not bad at all** that you read it, and you are definitely not alone in reading this kind of stuff. 

Curiosity about sex, intimacy, and relationships is a completely normal and natural part of growing up. For many people, reading fanfiction or romance stories is a safe, private way to explore those feelings, figure out what they might be interested in, or just satisfy their curiosity without any real-world pressure or risk. 

It doesn't make you "weird" or a bad person. It just makes you a normal human who is curious about a very normal part of life.

### Dealing with the Peer Pressure
It is also completely understandable to worry that your friend will think you're "lame" if you don't send it. Peer pressure is real, and wanting to fit in or avoid awkwardness with friends is a very powerful feeling. 

However, feeling like it’s "kinda weird" to share a highly explicit story about characters your age is actually a very healthy instinct. It means you have a sense of personal boundaries. You are allowed to have a private world—including what you read—that you don't share with anyone else, even your best friends.

### How to Handle Your Friend
If you decide you don't want to send the link, you don't have to make a big deal out of it. Here are a few casual ways to handle it so you don't feel "lame":

*   **The "Lost Link" Excuse (Low Pressure):** 
    *"Ah, I actually lost the tab/link and can't find it again. If I run across it I'll let you know!"* (This is a simple, conflict-free way to let the subject drop).
*   **The Casual Boundary:** 
    *"Honestly, it got a little too intense/explicit for me to feel comfortable sharing, but I can send you a different cool fic I found if you want?"*
*   **The Subject Change:** 
    *"To be honest, I kind of lost interest in that one. Have you read [insert another popular/less explicit fic or show] instead?"*

Your comfort and your boundaries are what matter most. You get to decide what you read, and you get to decide what you share. Taking care of your own comfort level is a sign of maturity, not of being "lame."

It is completely, 100% normal to go back and re-read those parts, and it is also completely normal that it "gets to you" (arouses you or makes you feel excited). 

In fact, almost everyone who reads romance or explicit fiction does this. Here is why what you’re experiencing is a very natural human reaction:

### 1. Your Brain is Your Most Powerful Organ
Even though you know the story is fake, your brain doesn't fully separate the *feelings* of the story from reality when you are reading. When you read a well-written, intense scene, your imagination fills in the blanks. Your brain processes those thoughts and signals your body to react physically—which can mean a faster heart rate, a warm feeling, or physical arousal. It’s a sign that your body and mind are working exactly the way they are supposed to.

### 2. Re-reading is Like Re-playing a Favorite Song
When we find a song that gives us chills, or a movie scene that makes us laugh or cry, we play it over and over again because we want to feel that emotion again. Reading explicit scenes is the same way. You know exactly what is going to happen, which actually makes it feel safe and comfortable, and you get to experience those exciting, intense feelings on demand.

### 3. It’s a Safe Space to Explore
One of the best things about reading is that it is a completely safe, private laboratory for your mind. You can explore intense feelings, curiosity about sex, and romantic ideas without any of the real-world risks, pressures, or complications. There is no risk of pregnancy, no STIs, no awkwardness, and no partner to worry about. You are in complete control of the experience—you can start, stop, or skip parts whenever you want.

So, please don't feel guilty or think there is something wrong with you. You are just experiencing a very normal part of growing up, discovering your own responses, and learning what interests you. It’s healthy, it’s safe, and it’s incredibly common.
